description: Cuts and keeps the segment between start and end, snapping both cut points to ZERO-CROSSINGS instead of splicing - the click-free cut with NO fades at all. Pinned to submode 1 (times in seconds); submode 2 takes sample counts (verified working). MONO only (stereo refused 'Application doesn't work with this type of infile.'). Duration model 'end - start' holds to within one sample: exact on a 440 Hz tone (0.5-1.5 -> 44100 frames), one frame short on noise (44099 - the crossing snap), exact via submode 2 sample counts. Unlike sfedit cut's SILENT bound swap, zcut WARNS: 'WARNING: end cut before startcut: reversing these times.' then swaps (output byte-identical to the ordered call). Deterministic.
musical_use: The splice-free surgical cut: because both edges land on zero-crossings there is no fade at either end - nothing is lost to a splice window - so it is the edit of choice before loop-building, wavecycle work (distort family) or any process where a 15 ms fade would soften the attack you are trying to keep. On periodic material the snap is inaudible and the cut is essentially sample-exact; on noisy material expect the bounds to move by up to a few samples to find a crossing. It is also the honest way to excerpt for measurement: no splice energy contaminates an RMS or spectrum reading. Needs mono input - split stereo first (housekeep chans) or use sfedit cut with splice 0 and accept the possible click.

start.description: Approximate time where the kept segment begins - CDP moves it to the nearest zero-crossing. Runtime-enforced 0 to the input duration. start > end is accepted WITH a warning ('WARNING: end cut before startcut: reversing these times.') and swapped - verified byte-identical to the ordered call; start == end refused 'endcut = startcut: No cutting possible.'. Breakpoint file refused ('Cannot read parameter 1 [...]: brkpnt_files not permitted.'). Required.

end.description: Approximate time where the kept segment ends, snapped to a zero-crossing. Runtime-enforced 0 to the input duration ('Parameter[2] Value (2.500000) out of range (0.000000 to 2.000000)' on a 2 s file - refused, not clamped). Output duration is end - start to within one sample. Breakpoint file refused ('Cannot read parameter 2 [...]'). Required.

examples.description: Click-free extraction of the middle second of a mono sound.
examples.expected_use: Output ~1.0 s (within a sample); both edges at zero-crossings, no fades anywhere - the interior is verbatim source.

known_issues: MONO ONLY: stereo refused 'Application doesn't work with this type of infile.' (exit 255).

Reversed bounds are swapped WITH a warning (unlike sfedit cut, which swaps silently) - 'WARNING: end cut before startcut: reversing these times.', output byte-identical to the ordered call. start == end refused 'endcut = startcut: No cutting possible.'.

Cut points move to the nearest zero-crossing, so the duration can be a sample or two off the requested span (verified: tone exact, noise -1 frame) and edge samples are whatever follows the crossing - on wideband noise the first sample can be large.
There is no splice parameter at all: no fades, no splice-length failure modes.
Both parameters reject breakpoint files ('Cannot read parameter N [...]: brkpnt_files not permitted.', N = 1-2). Deterministic (identical decoded shas 1.2 s apart).

Submode 2 (sample counts) verified working, uncurated. The multi-segment sibling 'sfedit zcuts' is engine-dropped: it writes one numbered file per time-pair ('<outstem>1.wav'...) and never creates the argv outfile - reach it via execute().
